nodes.name: Start
nodes.notes: Entry point of this sub-workflow. It is not run by hand: 'Collection · Main' calls it once per source and passes that source's settings (source name, raw table, file ID / sheet tab / API URL, run ID, batch size).

parameters.jsCode:
// Keep the source settings passed in by the main workflow and note the start time
return [{ json: { ...$input.first().json, started_at: Date.now() } }];

nodes.name: Init
nodes.notes: Keeps the source settings passed in by the main workflow and adds started_at (the current time), used later to work out how long the load took. Later nodes read their settings from here with $('Init').

parameters.query:
=-- Truncate and reload: running the collection twice never doubles the rows
TRUNCATE TABLE raw.{{ $json.table }};

nodes.name: Truncate raw table
nodes.notes: Empties raw.<table> before loading (TRUNCATE). This makes the workflow safe to re-run: a second run replaces the data instead of doubling it. Only the table for this source is emptied.

nodes.name: Download CSV from Drive
nodes.notes: Downloads the CSV from Google Drive, using the file ID set in the main workflow's 'Sources' node. Output is the file itself (binary), not rows yet. Needs the Google Drive credential.

nodes.name: Extract CSV rows
nodes.notes: Turns the CSV file into one item per row, using the first line as column names. 'Read As String' is on so values are not converted to numbers, which would drop leading zeros (e.g. zip 09790 → 9790). 'Include Empty Cells' is on so blank values are kept as empty text instead of disappearing.

nodes.name: Prepare rows
nodes.notes: Turns every value into text and adds _run_id. Nothing is trimmed, converted or fixed: the raw tables keep the data exactly as it arrived, mess included, for the cleaning workflow to find.

nodes.name: Insert in batches
nodes.notes: Loop Over Items. Sends the rows to Supabase a batch at a time (2,000 rows; 5,000 for geolocation) instead of all at once, which keeps memory use and query size down. 'loop' output = next batch to insert; 'done' output = all batches finished.

nodes.name: Insert into raw table
nodes.notes: Inserts the current batch into raw.<table>. Columns are mapped automatically, because the field names match the raw table's column names exactly. Loops back to 'Insert in batches' for the next batch.

nodes.name: Summarise
nodes.notes: Builds the log row for this load: rows read from the source vs rows written to Supabase, how long it took, and status. Status is 'warning' if the two counts differ, which means a batch failed quietly.

nodes.name: Write agent log
nodes.notes: Writes the load's log row into ops.agent_logs (FR-C4). One row per source per run.

nodes.name: Return result
nodes.notes: Returns one short summary item to the main workflow. The loaded rows themselves are never returned, because sending a million rows back would use a lot of memory.
